what: §7.3a 'lose the car with two detached' (P1-S04c; the loose-wheel-drive row is the other half): a car at 12 m/s on the main straight loses its front left and rear right wheels on the same tick. Two detached wheels wreck it: every remaining part pops off as debris, its chassis stays on the track as a husk (a dynamic body), and the player is back at their anchor, upright on a fresh intact car with the same identity, after the 2 s hold. Baselines: no input and mashing wreck it just the same, so what differs is the deliberate run driving the fresh car off its anchor again once the hold is over.

§7.3a 'get back onto the route from ... a debris pile' (P1-S04c): a car at rest on the main straight with seven 0.8 m blocks of debris (77 kg each, dynamic, as wrecked parts are) heaped around it: two rows of two in front, two beside it and one behind. A deliberate full-throttle drive shoves its way out of the pile and away along the road (14 m or more in 10 s; the same drive with an empty road covers about 60) upright and unwrecked; no input stays in the pile.

§7.3a: the player can always recover from out of bounds (0.1's oob-recovery lesson). Four cars are thrown out a second into a race: past +X, past −Z, under the kill plane inside the bounds, and off the far edge at 40 m/s. Each is wrecked once and respawned at its anchor (the grid slot; no gate passed yet), upright on its wheels. Each wreck leaves its chassis behind as a husk (P1-S04c): four husks, dynamic bodies, none despawned.

§7.3a: the player can always recover from a flip. Five cars land inverted (roof or side) at separate points of the greybox. No input (the assist alone), held throttle, mashing, and the Recover button all end upright on four wheels; Recover does it through the 2 s respawn. Car 5 is the backstop (P1-S04c): the assist is forced to fail at 7 s (a wreck command, as the stuck-flip rule would issue at 3 s), so it is wrecked, leaves a husk (the only one: the other four never wreck) and respawns upright at its anchor.

§7.3a 'keep driving with one loose wheel' (P1-S04b): car 0's front left wheel is loose (health 10 of 80, so it loses 15 % of its friction slip) while car 1's wheels are all intact; both roll at 15 m/s on the main straight, 4 m either side of the centreline, with the same inputs: a little throttle, full left lock from 1 s to 2 s, then straight. The loose-wheel car keeps its speed, stays upright on all four wheels, and still steers with authority (within a few degrees of the intact car's heading change). Baselines: no input doesn't turn; mashing doesn't end where the deliberate drive does.
